meta.source: U.S. Census Bureau, State Population Totals, Vintage 2025 (which states get a page); U.S. Energy Information Administration, 2020 Residential Energy Consumption Survey (RECS), Highlights for water heating in U.S. homes by state; state energy offices (rebate status)
meta.notes: One record per state cost page (/water-heater-installation-cost/{slug}/), the 10 most populous states by the Census Vintage 2025 estimate (POPESTIMATE2025). Other states stay unbuilt until Search Console shows these 10 index and rank (PHASES.md 6c). waterHeating = EIA RECS 2020, main water heating fuel, share of occupied homes; a share EIA withholds (Q) or has no sample for (N) is left out. rebate = the state's federally funded Home Energy Rebates appliance program (HEEHR, formerly HEAR) as its official page described it on rebate.checked; status is our one-word summary of that quote: open, limited, closed, notLaunched or unconfirmed (official page could not be opened from our checker). Review rebates every three months with data/incentives.json. Costs, prices and inlet temperatures are not stored here: they come from the shared cost model and the state data files (npm run build:data).

rebate.summary: Phase I paid only for heat pump HVAC systems, not water heaters, and its money is fully reserved. Phase II has not been announced.

notes.heading: California requires earthquake straps
notes.text: California law requires every new and replacement water heater to be anchored or strapped so it cannot fall in an earthquake, and home sellers must certify that the water heater is braced. Budget for straps on any California replacement; in the calculator they are part of the code items extra.
notes.quote: New and replacement water heaters are required by law to be anchored or strapped to resist falling during earthquakes. Home sellers must certify to buyers that water heaters are braced.

notes.heading: California's energy code applies to a replacement too
notes.text: Title 24, Part 6, California's energy code, is not only for new homes: a replacement water heater must meet its prescriptive water heating rules as well as federal standards, and the permit inspection is where that gets checked. A heat pump water heater is one of the allowed routes for a gas home, which is part of why California utilities pay some of the largest heat pump rebates in the table below.
notes.source: BayREN, Residential Water Heaters: Guide to 2022 Energy Code Requirements
notes.quote: The Standards require all new or replacement water heaters to meet certain energy specifications.

local.heading: What makes a California replacement different
paras: Three things set California apart. Gas still heats water in {gasPct}% of homes, yet the state's energy code and its utilities both push toward heat pumps, so a gas-to-heat-pump switch is a common quote here and comes to about ${hpGas.typical} installed. Earthquake straps are a legal must on every replacement, not an optional extra.

Mild weather helps every type. Incoming water averages {inletAnnual} °F and only falls to about {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}, so a heat pump in a garage rarely meets the cold air that cuts its efficiency, and a tankless unit loses only about {seasonLossPct}% of its flow from summer to winter.

rebate.program: Texas Home Energy Rebates (HOMES and HEARS)
rebate.quote: Current Status (Updated August 21, 2026) Rebates are not currently available.
rebate.summary: The programs are still being designed, and a launch date will be set once the state has DOE approval. SECO advises against signing anything tied to these rebates before they launch.

notes.heading: Houston requires a permit pulled by a master plumber
notes.text: In Houston, the state's largest city, a plumbing permit is required to replace a water heater, and only a master plumber registered with the city can obtain it. A single-family home needs no plan review. Texas licenses plumbers statewide through the State Board of Plumbing Examiners, so ask for the license number on the quote and check it on the board's site.
notes.quote: A plumbing permit is required for the replacement and installation of water heaters. Conditions & Exceptions Plan review is not needed if installed at a single family residence. Permit must be obtained by a master plumber registered with the City of Houston.

local.heading: What makes a Texas replacement different
paras: Texas leans electric, but not by much: {electricPct}% of homes heat water with electricity and {gasPct}% with gas, so check which you have before you compare quotes. Labor here is priced below the national level, which keeps a plain gas tank near ${g50.typical}.

Warm ground water is the other Texas advantage. Incoming water averages {inletAnnual} °F, and even in {coldMonth} it stays near {inletWinter} °F, so a single whole-house tankless unit keeps up with more of a family's morning than it would up north. A heat pump in a hot garage also works well, as long as the space stays inside ENERGY STAR's {hpLowF} to {hpHighF} °F range.

rebate.program: Florida Energy Saver Program (HOMES and HEEHR)
rebate.agency: Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Office of Energy
rebate.quote: The High-Efficiency Electric Home Rebates (HEEHR) and Home Owner Managing Energy Savings (HOMES) programs are expected to launch in the future.
rebate.summary: Neither program takes applications yet. The portal lets you register for news on the timeline.

notes.heading: Miami-Dade sets a flat fee for a water heater change-out
notes.text: Miami-Dade County's building department lists an exact change-out of a water heater as its own permit line, at $130 per heater, with a higher rate for larger tanks. That is a real, published permit fee you can hold a quote against; other Florida counties and cities set their own fees, and our statewide figure uses a national permit range instead.
notes.source: Miami-Dade County Building Department, plumbing and gas fee schedule
notes.quote: P045 Exact change out of water heater $130.00/heater

local.heading: What makes a Florida replacement different
paras: Florida is an electric state: {electricPct}% of homes heat water with electricity, the highest share among the states we cover, so most jobs are an electric tank swapped for another or for a heat pump. Natural gas reaches only {gasPct}% of homes, mostly where a gas utility such as Peoples Gas runs mains.

The climate suits a heat pump. Incoming water averages {inletAnnual} °F and stays near {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}, and garages rarely fall below the {hpLowF} °F point where a heat pump switches to its backup elements. Against a standard electric tank it saves about ${hpSave} a year here.

rebate.program: New York Home Energy Rebates (HER and HEAR)
rebate.summary: NYSERDA's rebate pages refused our checker on the check date, so we could not confirm what is open today. Ask NYSERDA or check the ENERGY STAR Rebate Finder before you count on a rebate.

notes.heading: In New York City, a Licensed Master Plumber files the work
notes.text: New York City's Department of Buildings has a Licensed Master Plumber obtain plumbing permits and arrange the inspection. Its form for a gas water heater replacement has the plumber certify that the appliance valve was not moved, the chimney is sound and no gas piping was installed or replaced, so a swap that changes the gas line or vent becomes a bigger filing.
notes.source: NYC Department of Buildings, OP128 Heat and Hot Water certification and Plumbing Permits page
notes.quote: If I am working on the replacement of a gas-fired boiler, water heater, or furnace with a capacity of not more than 350,000 BTUs, I certify that the appliance valve has not been moved, the chimney is in good working condition, and no gas piping has been installed/replaced

local.heading: What makes a New York replacement different
paras: New York has the mix most other states lack: {gasPct}% of homes heat water with gas, {electricPct}% with electricity and {fuelOilPct}% still with fuel oil, often from the heating boiler. Prices also run high, so labor on a gas tank is about ${laborG} and a 50-gallon gas job comes to about ${g50.typical}.

Winters are long. Incoming water falls to about {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}, so a whole-house tankless unit delivers only about {gpmW} gallons per minute then. That is why New York utilities, led by Con Edison's instant rebate, focus their money on heat pump tanks rather than tankless units.

rebate.quote: On June 1st, 2026, the Department of Energy released new program guidance. EPO is currently working to understand these changes, make the necessary changes to program design to be in compliance, and launch the program for consumers in the Commonwealth.
rebate.summary: The program is being redesigned after DOE's June 2026 guidance and is not open to homeowners yet.

notes.heading: Philadelphia requires a master plumber and a signed certification
notes.text: Philadelphia's Department of Licenses and Inspections issues the plumbing permit, and a licensed master plumber must oversee the work. After the install, the city's Water Heater Replacement Certification form records the permit number, the master plumber's license, the tank's size, make and model, and confirms the work meets Chapter 5 of the Philadelphia Plumbing Code.
notes.source: City of Philadelphia, Get a plumbing permit; Water Heater Replacement Certification Form (TP-022-F)
notes.quote: A licensed master plumber must oversee plumbing work.

local.heading: What makes a Pennsylvania replacement different
paras: Pennsylvania splits between fuels: {gasPct}% of homes heat water with gas, {electricPct}% with electricity and {fuelOilPct}% with fuel oil. Gas is the cheaper tank to run here, about ${gYear} a year against ${eYear} for a standard electric tank, so a heat pump mainly pays off in homes that already have electric water heat.

Pennsylvania's utility rebates come from its Act 129 efficiency programs, which run in multi-year phases; PPL's page notes a program change after May 2026, so check the current phase before you count on an amount. Incoming water drops to about {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}.

rebate.quote: At this time, the Illinois EPA's IRA Section 50122 Home Electrification and Appliance Rebate Program, or HEAR Rebate Program, application has not yet been processed by USDOE or provided to Illinois EPA for administration or distribution.
rebate.summary: The appliance rebate has not launched. Illinois says it plans to give the first rebates to low-income households and will not pay rebates for work done before launch.

notes.heading: Chicago spells out how a replacement must be connected
notes.text: In Chicago, the work must be done by the Chicago-licensed plumbing contractor or the homeowner named on the permit. The city's permit terms for replacing a water heater are specific: a listed and labeled unit installed to the maker's instructions, unions at the connections (dielectric ones between different metals), a full-port shutoff on the cold line and no valve on the hot side, and a relief valve outlet that is not piped straight into the drain system.
notes.source: City of Chicago Department of Buildings, Express Permit Program terms: plumbing work
notes.quote: Plumbing work must be performed by the Chicago-licensed plumbing contractor or homeowner listed on the permit application.

local.heading: What makes an Illinois replacement different
paras: Illinois is a gas state: {gasPct}% of homes heat water with natural gas, and gas is cheap here at ${therm} per therm, so a gas tank costs only about ${gYear} a year to run. That makes a gas-to-gas swap the usual job, and the gas utility rebate is small.

Cold winters shape the tankless choice. Incoming water falls to about {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}, the coldest month, and a whole-house tankless unit then gives about {gpmW} gallons per minute. A heat pump tank in an unheated basement can also drop below ENERGY STAR's {hpLowF} °F limit in a hard winter, so check the space before you buy one.

rebate.program: Ohio Home Energy Rebates (HOMES and HEEHR)
rebate.summary: We could not find a current status page from the Ohio Department of Development on the check date, and third-party trackers disagree. Ask the department or check the ENERGY STAR Rebate Finder before you count on a rebate.

notes.heading: Cleveland requires a permit for a replaced water heater
notes.text: Cleveland's Division of Construction Permitting lists new or replaced water heaters among the jobs that need a plumbing permit, and gas or water piping may also need a separate permit from the city's Division of Water. Ohio sets the residential code statewide, but each city or county building department runs its own permits and fees.
notes.source: City of Cleveland, Department of Building and Housing: plumbing permits
notes.quote: Permits are also necessary for new, extended, or repaired gas service, water service, plumbing systems and fixtures, and new or replaced water heaters.

local.heading: What makes an Ohio replacement different
paras: Ohio leans gas: {gasPct}% of homes heat water with natural gas and {electricPct}% with electricity, and gas is priced at ${therm} per therm. Utility help is thinner than in most states we cover: Columbia Gas of Ohio has ended its residential efficiency rebates except for income-qualified weatherization, and the state's federal rebate status could not be confirmed.

Incoming water drops to about {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}, so plan a tankless unit for winter flow, and check that a basement heat pump location stays above {hpLowF} °F. A plain gas tank, about ${g50.typical} installed, stays the cheapest to own over {years} years.

rebate.program: Georgia's Home Energy Rebates (HER and HEAR)
rebate.quote: The HEAR program for single-family has reopened with limited measures.
rebate.summary: The reopened appliance rebate is limited to wiring and panel upgrades done with a whole-home efficiency (HER) project, so it does not pay for a heat pump water heater on its own.

notes.heading: Metro Atlanta cities treat a water heater swap as permit work
notes.text: Georgia leaves permits to each city and county. Peachtree Corners, in Gwinnett County north of Atlanta, lists water heater replacement on its building department's short list of jobs that need a permit, alongside new plumbing fixtures that alter piping. Expect the same in most metro Atlanta jurisdictions, and ask your installer whose permit covers the job, because a gas unit also gets its gas line and vent inspected.
notes.source: City of Peachtree Corners, When Do I Need a Building Permit

local.heading: What makes a Georgia replacement different
paras: Georgia is an electric-leaning state: {electricPct}% of homes heat water with electricity and {gasPct}% with gas. Georgia Power's rebate of up to ${r:georgiapower-hpwh} for a heat pump water heater, paid when a program-affiliated installer does the job, is the main money on offer, because the state's federal appliance rebate is limited.

Mild winters help. Incoming water averages {inletAnnual} °F and falls only to about {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}, so a heat pump in a garage spends little time on its backup elements. Against a standard electric tank it saves about ${hpSave} a year here.

rebate.program: Energy Saver North Carolina (HOMES and HEAR)
rebate.agency: NC Department of Environmental Quality, State Energy Office
rebate.quote: Up to $1,750 for an ENERGY STAR-certified electric heat pump water heater.
rebate.summary: The appliance rebate covers heat pump water heaters for households with income up to 150% of the area median, installed by a program contractor. Applications start at energysavernc.org.

notes.heading: North Carolina law can waive the permit for a like-for-like swap
notes.text: North Carolina's General Assembly exempted one- and two-family homes from a plumbing permit for a replacement water heater, but only when a licensed plumber does the job, examines it and leak-tests the gas piping, and the new unit uses no more energy and keeps the same fuel, location, capacity and venting. Any change, such as gas to heat pump, brings the permit back. Counties such as Wake publish the same rule.
notes.source: North Carolina General Assembly, Session Law 2013-160
notes.quote: a permit shall not be required for the connection of a water heater that is being replaced, provided that the work is performed by a person licensed under G.S. 87-21, who personally examines the work at completion and ensures that a leak test has been performed on the gas piping

local.heading: What makes a North Carolina replacement different
paras: North Carolina is one of the few states we cover where the federal appliance rebate is open: Energy Saver North Carolina pays up to ${r:nc-hear-hpwh} toward a heat pump water heater for income-qualified homes, installed by a program-registered contractor.

Most homes here heat water with electricity ({electricPct}%), and state law lets a licensed plumber swap like for like without a permit. Incoming water averages {inletAnnual} °F and drops to about {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}, mild enough that a heat pump in a garage holds most of its savings, about ${hpSave} a year against a standard electric tank.

rebate.program: Michigan Home Energy Rebates (MiHER: HER and HEAR)
rebate.quote: Governor Gretchen Whitmer announced the statewide launch of the Michigan Home Energy Rebates Program (MiHER)
rebate.summary: Michigan launched its rebates statewide in April 2025, including the appliance rebate for income-qualified homes. EGLE's own site refused our checker, so we could not confirm how much money is left today.

notes.heading: Michigan lets a homeowner pull the plumbing permit
notes.text: Michigan's Bureau of Construction Codes issues plumbing permits to a licensed plumbing contractor or to a homeowner doing their own plumbing. If you hire someone, the permit should carry that contractor's license number; a gas water heater also involves mechanical work, so ask whether the contractor holds both licenses.
notes.source: Michigan LARA, Bureau of Construction Codes: plumbing permit information
notes.quote: To obtain plumbing permits, an applicant shall be a licensed plumbing contractor or a homeowner installing his/her own plumbing, building sewer, or private sewer.

local.heading: What makes a Michigan replacement different
paras: Michigan has the coldest water of the states we cover: incoming water falls to about {inletWinter} °F in {coldMonth}, and a whole-house tankless unit then manages about {gpmW} gallons per minute. Size for that month, or keep a tank. Gas heats water in {gasPct}% of homes and is cheap at ${therm} per therm.

Electricity is the expensive fuel here, about {kwhCents} cents per kWh, so a standard electric tank costs about ${eYear} a year to run. Both big utilities, DTE and Consumers Energy, offer instant discounts on heat pump water heaters through contractors rather than mail-in checks.
